question: What is the most common developmental complication in bacterial meningitis in the pediatric age?
reasoning_chain: CHAIN: "Bacterial meningitis" -> "inflammation of meninges" -> "damage to cochlea or auditory nerve" -> "hearing loss" -> 95%
CHAIN: "Bacterial meningitis" -> "inflammation of meninges" -> "increased intracranial pressure" -> "possible hydrocephalus" -> 70%
CHAIN: "Bacterial meningitis" -> "inflammation of meninges" -> "cerebral damage" -> "residual epilepsy" -> 60%
CHAIN: "Bacterial meningitis" -> "inflammation of meninges" -> "cognitive impairment" -> "mental retardation" -> 50%
CHAIN: "Bacterial meningitis" -> "inflammation of meninges" -> "optic nerve damage" -> "visual defects" -> 40%
analysis: Hearing loss is the most common developmental complication following bacterial meningitis in children. This is due to the potential damage to the cochlea and auditory pathways caused by the infection and inflammation. While other complications like residual epilepsy, mental retardation, hydrocephalus, and visual defects can occur, they are less common compared to hearing loss.
